dedupe_keys.name: auction based liquidity saving mechanisms tested on four rtgs systems bis working paper 1318

description: This case study designs and tests a new liquidity-saving mechanism for real-time gross settlement (RTGS) payment systems, in which participants bid in auctions to supply liquidity that lets a set of queued payments settle, with side payments from liquidity receivers to providers. It contrasts with conventional queue-based mechanisms that net payments using liquidity already committed. It was carried out by Rodney Garratt, Morten Linnemann Bech, Marko Nanut Petrič and Caner Ates and published by the Bank for International Settlements as Working Paper 1318 on 16 December 2025. The mechanism is evaluated with agent-based simulations calibrated on transaction data from four RTGS systems: BCRP-RTGS in Peru, SAMOS and SADC-RTGS in South Africa, and SIC in Switzerland. The 29-page paper is free as a PDF under BIS terms. Across all trials auctions succeeded 79% of the time on average, from 62 to 100%, and failed auctions typically did not raise liquidity usage. Caveats: it is a working paper, the transaction data are not published, and results depend on the bidding behaviour assumed for agents. For simulation it is a worked example of agent-based testing of payment system design choices on real transaction flows, relevant to how settlement systems economise on liquidity and cope with stress. It is related to the ECB TARGET2 liquidity stress test case study record in this catalogue.
